name: Singapore
headline: Singapore: +5.0% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 166% of GDP
sections: Singapore is a $604 billion economy (2025), the world's 29th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.0% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $163K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 17.4% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 166% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has risen from 147% in 2020. The general government balance is +4.2% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +16.7% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 320% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 26.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 169% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.3 years (2024). Population: 6.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
